findings.claim: In February 2023 OSHA fined Mars Wrigley $14,502 for a serious violation after two contractor workers fell into a partially filled chocolate tank at its Elizabethtown, Pennsylvania plant in June 2022. OSHA said the workers were not authorised to enter the tank and had not been trained on its safety procedures.

A November 2023 CBS News investigation reported children, some as young as five, working on every Ghanaian farm it visited that supplies Mars, and found names on Mars-linked child labour monitoring lists that were inaccurate or fabricated. Mars said it condemns child labour, was not given details in advance, and that more needs to be done.

In December 2017 the FTC finalised a consent order requiring Mars to divest 12 specialty and emergency veterinary clinics as a condition of its $9.1 billion acquisition of VCA, after alleging the deal would lessen competition in 10 US localities. This was a negotiated order, not a court finding.

Mars reports a 16.9% absolute cut in value-chain greenhouse gas emissions from 2015 to 2025 and a 42.6% cut in Scope 1 and 2, against a target of 50% for the value chain by 2030. The figures are self-reported, and neither source cites independent assurance.

ecology.reason: Mars is a global food, confectionery and pet care group, a material footprint under the rubric. It reports a 16.9% absolute cut in value-chain emissions since 2015, self-reported and well short of its 50% target for 2030. No major environmental incident was checked or found.

social.reason: OSHA fined Mars Wrigley in 2023 after two untrained contractor workers fell into a chocolate tank at its Pennsylvania plant. CBS News reported in 2023 child labour on Ghanaian farms supplying Mars and flawed monitoring lists; Mars condemned child labour. No official child labour finding against Mars was found.

legal.reason: Regulatory actions at company level: an FTC consent order requiring divestment of 12 veterinary clinics to clear the VCA purchase (2017) and an OSHA penalty of $14,502 (2023). No court finding or personal matter was found.

unresolved.reason: Mars is privately held and family-controlled, with limited disclosure. CBS News reporting in 2023 questioned the accuracy of child labour monitoring lists in Mars's Ghana supply chain; this rests on reporting, not an official finding. No pending case against Mars was found in this check.

proposal.counterweights: Mars reports a 16.9% absolute cut in value-chain emissions since 2015, against a 50% target for 2030; the figures are self-reported.
proposal.rationale: Legal 0 to 1: the FTC divestiture order and an OSHA penalty are regulatory actions naming Mars.
